active_paradigms.idea: Replace the staged hierarchy with a single global capacitated min-cost-flow placement model
active_paradigms.description: The current program first locks contiguous logical-expert groups to nodes using LPT-style greedy packing, then independently chooses replicas inside each node, and finally greedily packs copies onto GPUs. Its strength is that every stage enforces exact capacities and descending greedy ordering gives a reasonable fast approximation. Its main weakness is irrevocability: a bad group-to-node choice prevents a hot expert from using spare capacity elsewhere, and the replica decision is made before knowing its eventual GPU placement. Construct one directed flow graph per layer with source-to-expert arcs enforcing one mandatory base copy plus optional copy units, expert-to-GPU arcs for allowed placements, and GPU-to-sink capacity equal to physical experts per GPU. Encode node/group restrictions as absent arcs or large penalties, rather than committing to a group permutation before placement. Give each optional kth copy of expert e a marginal benefit based on reducing its ideal per-copy load from weight[e]/(k-1) to weight[e]/k, and give GPU sink increments increasing convex congestion costs; the flow then chooses both replica counts and locations jointly. Convert each selected expert-to-GPU unit into the required physical slot ordering and construct ranks by occurrence order. This is fundamentally different from the failed Hungarian repair because it jointly chooses replicas and placements rather than assigning a fixed set of replicas after the fact. The supplied adapter exposes only combined_score and hides the original metric implementation, so calibrate congestion and hierarchy penalties against the actual evaluator source before committing to a cost formula.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly reduce the worst GPU and node load induced by both replica-count allocation and copy placement, eliminating losses from the current three irreversible greedy stages; use it only where its runtime remains below the evaluator timeout.
active_paradigms.cautions: Use integral integer costs and integer capacities; costs must be nonnegative after any benefit offset. Preserve mandatory coverage of every logical expert, exact GPU capacities, and the expected phy2log/phranks scatter invariants. A plain linear sum-of-load cost is not sufficient if the hidden evaluator scores a maximum or imbalance; approximate that objective with sharply increasing GPU overload increments. Do not use scipy.optimize.milp or linear_sum_assignment, both of which have already failed; this is a graph-flow formulation with nonlinear behavior represented by discrete parallel arcs.

active_paradigms.idea: Apply bottleneck local-search moves that optimize the evaluator-relevant maximum load after the greedy construction
active_paradigms.description: Keep the existing greedy solution as a guaranteed feasible initialization, because it is fast and already achieves the reported score. The important current defect is not feasibility but that balanced_packing has no repair phase: LPT can leave a large final imbalance whenever a heavy copy is assigned early to a pack that later receives several medium copies. For each layer, maintain GPU loads, node loads, replica counts, and a reverse map of physical copies. Repeatedly identify the current bottleneck GPU/node and test only constant-time feasible neighborhood moves: move one copy to a lower-loaded GPU in the same node, swap copies across GPUs, transfer one optional replica from an underutilized expert to an overloaded one, or move a complete group when hierarchy permits. Accept a move only when the lexicographic objective improves: first maximum GPU load, then maximum node load, then sum of squared GPU loads; this matches bottleneck balancing much better than the current sum-oriented heap packing. Use a bounded best-improvement pass and stop when an entire pass produces no strict improvement, so runtime is predictable rather than depending on hard instances. Recompute the final physical ordering and ranks only once after moves complete. This directly addresses the staged greedy algorithm's local mistakes without revisiting the failed MILP, Hungarian assignment, or top-k replica-selection approaches.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary load-balance component by reducing the peak physical-expert/GPU load and tail imbalance while retaining the current solution as a lower-risk baseline; bounded neighborhoods also control algorithm execution time.
active_paradigms.cautions: The acceptance calculation must use the same effective copy load convention as the evaluator, normally weight[e]/replica_count[e], and must update all copies of an expert when its count changes. Never temporarily remove the sole copy of an expert, violate per-GPU slot counts, or change output tensor shapes. Limit candidates to bottleneck-related GPUs and maintain sorted load structures, otherwise exhaustive swap enumeration becomes quadratic or worse. Since the evaluator code shown delegates scoring to a hidden original evaluator, verify whether it measures node traffic separately before allowing cross-node moves.

active_paradigms.idea: Use deterministic best-fit-decreasing packing with ordered residual capacities instead of minimum-current-load LPT
active_paradigms.description: The current balanced_packing is classic descending LPT with a min-heap, plus a hard item-count limit per pack. This is fast and sensible, but choosing the currently least-loaded pack ignores the fact that each pack has a fixed remaining number of slots: it can strand medium-heavy items in the last slots and create avoidable final maxima. For each layer and each packing stage, process descending weights as now, but choose among packs with remaining slots the feasible destination whose post-placement load is closest below a candidate target makespan; when no pack fits below target, choose the smallest resulting overload. Find the target by deterministic feasibility checks over the lower bound max(total_load/num_packs, largest_item) and an upper bound from the existing LPT result, then perform the final assignment at the best target. An ordered residual-capacity structure permits selecting the predecessor/successor residual in logarithmic time rather than scanning all packs. Apply this same routine to group-to-node packing and physical-copy-to-GPU packing, leaving the successful hierarchy, output semantics, and replica heuristic untouched. This is a low-risk change because every generated assignment still has exactly groups_per_pack items per pack and it improves the actual bottleneck packing criterion rather than only vectorizing the existing replica rule. It is distinct from the failed torch.topk experiment, which only changed how replica marginal choices were selected and did not repair either packing stage.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce makespan at both node and GPU packing stages, especially adversarial distributions with a few large and many medium experts, while improving or preserving runtime through logarithmic destination lookup.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not treat a lower-bound feasibility test as valid unless it enforces both load and exact cardinality constraints; item-count constraints are why ordinary bin-packing checks can produce invalid layouts. Use stable tie-breaking by pack index for reproducibility and retain the current LPT assignment whenever the target-based assignment is worse. Float weights should be compared with a small tolerance, and any tensor/device conversion overhead must not dominate the small evaluator instances. The global fallback behavior for num_groups not divisible by num_nodes must remain unchanged.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace the staged greedy hierarchy with a per-layer bottleneck MILP using scipy.optimize.milp
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first greedily assigns fixed logical groups to nodes, then greedily allocates replicas independently inside each node, and finally greedily packs resulting copies onto GPUs. This is fast and preserves all cardinality constraints, but each irreversible stage optimizes a surrogate objective and cannot correct a poor earlier node/group decision. Formulate one per-layer mixed-integer bottleneck model whose binary variable assigns each physical GPU slot to a logical expert, with exactly the required number of slots per GPU and at least one copy for every expert. Add replica-count variables and a makespan variable T, enforcing that the traffic assigned to every GPU, computed as the sum of expert load divided by that expert's chosen replica count, is at most T. If hierarchical locality is required, forbid assignments outside the node selected for each group, or add an explicit group-to-node binary assignment with exact groups-per-node constraints. Use the current greedy result as an incumbent-derived upper bound on T and impose that bound before calling scipy.optimize.milp, so the solver only searches for an actual improvement. Use a small positive secondary objective on replica count imbalance or on traffic variance after minimizing T, rather than optimizing only an arbitrary expert ordering. This directly targets the likely evaluator bottleneck metric instead of separately balancing group totals, replica loads, and GPU totals.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary load-balance score: reduce the maximum physical-GPU load, especially cases where the current group-to-node partition strands a hot expert in an overloaded node. Use the greedy incumbent as a quality baseline and reject solver output unless its realized max load improves it.
tried_paradigms.cautions: MILP can be too slow for large expert counts or many layers, so apply it only below a conservative size threshold and retain the current greedy algorithm as a timeout-safe fallback. The load contribution must use the final replica count, requiring standard binary-count linking variables or enumeration of allowable replica counts; a naive linear model that treats copy load as weight/count without linking is invalid. Preserve the evaluator's exact output invariants: every logical expert must have rank-0, ranks must be contiguous, every GPU must receive exactly num_replicas/num_gpus slots, and node restrictions must not be silently violated.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use a one-shot Hungarian assignment repair to place fixed replicas into GPU slots
tried_paradigms.description: Keep the current replica-count decision initially, but replace the final descending greedy physical-expert packing with a global slot assignment solved by scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment. Expand each GPU into its fixed number of physical-expert slots, and build a cost matrix between each replica copy and each allowable slot. Derive the cost from the greedy placement's leave-one-copy-out GPU load: for placing copy p of load a on GPU g, use a convex overload penalty such as max(0, base_load[g] + a - target)^2 plus a much smaller total-load penalty. Set an effectively infinite cost for slots on a different node, thereby retaining the current hierarchy and communication locality. One Hungarian call then jointly chooses all replica-to-GPU assignments within the cardinality constraints, unlike the current list/heap procedure whose early heavy placements are never reconsidered. Reconstruct physical-to-logical order and per-logical ranks from the selected slot assignment. This is particularly useful when many similarly heavy replicas exist: greedy LPT is good but can make avoidable tie-driven imbalances, while assignment gives a globally consistent repair under the chosen local linearization.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: GPU-level tail load and variance after replication, without changing the number of replicas or group/node allocation. This is a bounded-cost quality improvement over the current final packing stage and can improve score where imbalance is caused by placement rather than insufficient replication.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The Hungarian cost is a linearized surrogate because true GPU load is coupled across all assigned copies; compute base_load by removing the source copy from its incumbent GPU to avoid charging it twice. Use a finite but safely dominant forbidden cost rather than infinity if the backend rejects infinities. Its cubic matrix cost can exceed greedy packing for large numbers of replicas, so gate it to small-to-medium per-node replica counts and compare the realized maximum load against the incumbent before accepting it.

tried_paradigms.idea: Vectorize greedy replica allocation exactly through marginal-copy selection with torch.topk
tried_paradigms.description: The current replicate_experts loop performs one full max reduction over all logical experts for every redundant physical slot, which is costly when many extra replicas are available. Its selection rule has a useful exact characterization: allocating the k-th total copy of expert i is selected in descending order of the marginal next-copy load weight[i]/k, for k starting at 2. Build once the candidate tensor weight[:, :, None] divided by k=2 through num_redundant+1, flatten its expert-and-k dimensions, and select the num_redundant largest candidates per layer with torch.topk. Count selected candidates for each expert to obtain logcnt, then create phy2log and ranks in vectorized form from those counts. Because weight[i]/k is monotone decreasing in k, selecting top marginal values automatically satisfies the prefix property: no third copy can be selected without its second copy, apart from harmless equal-value tie choices. Thus the resulting replica counts minimize the same greedy water-filling criterion as the iterative routine, while eliminating repeated max/scatter updates and Python-level iteration. The saved execution time can be spent on a modest final placement refinement or directly improve any evaluator component that rewards rearrangement latency.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Algorithm execution time while preserving the current algorithm's replica-count quality exactly; it also makes behavior more deterministic by defining tie handling through a single top-k ordering. This addresses the efficiency half of the objective without risking a worse balance caused by a new heuristic.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The candidate tensor has O(num_logical_experts * num_redundant) entries per layer, so only use it when this is smaller than the work and memory budget of repeated reductions; retain the existing loop for extremely large redundant counts. Floating-point ties can produce a different but equally balanced expert choice than heap/argmax, so ensure deterministic top-k behavior if evaluator reproducibility matters. Do not accidentally select k=1 candidates: every logical expert already has its mandatory original copy, and only k>=2 corresponds to a redundant slot.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace greedy GPU packing with a bottleneck-oriented linear assignment of physical replicas to fixed GPU slots
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first greedily assigns groups to nodes, greedily chooses replica counts within each node, then greedily packs resulting physical replicas onto GPUs. Its main strength is that every stage preserves exact capacities and it is extremely cheap: descending list scheduling gives reasonable balancing without a combinatorial search. Its principal weakness is that the final `balanced_packing` stage is irreversible greedy LPT: a large replica placed early can prevent a much better global permutation of all replicas across equal-capacity GPU slots. After retaining the current node grouping and replica counts, construct one assignment problem per layer and node whose left side is the physical replicas and whose right side is the fixed physical-expert positions, grouped by GPU. Derive a cost matrix from a target GPU load, for example a strongly increasing penalty for putting a replica of effective load `weight[e]/count[e]` into a GPU whose already-reserved slot load would exceed the target; use several identical slot columns per GPU with increasing marginal penalties. Solve the complete permutation in one call to `scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment`, then emit `phy2log` in the assigned physical-position order and retain ranks/counts exactly as in the current implementation. This directly improves the placement decision without changing output semantics or introducing invalid mappings. It is especially attractive when each node has a modest number of GPUs and experts, because dense assignment is predictable and avoids Python heap/list conversions.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce the largest and high-percentile per-GPU effective expert load after replication, the likely load-balance component of the primary score, while preserving the current algorithm's replication quality and fixed expert-per-GPU capacity.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The evaluator wrapper shown does not expose the original evaluator's scalar formula, so confirm whether it measures maximum GPU load, variance, inter-node traffic, runtime, or a combination before choosing the penalty shape. Plain linear assignment minimizes additive cost rather than exact makespan; use convex increasing slot costs calibrated from the current greedy target, not merely cost equal to replica load. Keep assignments node-local when hierarchy is required, and ensure `phyrank` remains the occurrence rank for its selected logical expert so `log2phy.scatter_` remains collision-free. Dense assignment can be more expensive than heaps on large instances, so gate it to small per-node replica counts and retain greedy packing as a fallback.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use an exact capacitated min-cost-flow formulation to jointly choose replica destinations under GPU capacity
tried_paradigms.description: The current algorithm allocates redundant copies independently inside each node before deciding their GPU locations. This is fast and sensible because it assigns additional copies to the largest current per-copy load, but it cannot recognize that a replica is only valuable if it can be placed on a GPU whose aggregate load is low. Formulate each layer/node as an integral flow network: expert-copy choices supply physical-expert units, GPU position/marginal-load arcs enforce exactly `phy_experts_per_gpu` copies per GPU, and each expert-to-GPU arc represents placing one copy with its resulting per-copy token load. Encode load balancing with a separable convex approximation: split each GPU's load budget into increasing-cost marginal arcs, so sending a high-load copy to an already-loaded GPU incurs sharply higher cost. Include mandatory first-copy arcs for every logical expert and optional replica arcs, with total flow equal to the physical-expert count, so all logical experts remain represented and the exact replica budget is consumed. A single `networkx.min_cost_flow` call yields integral copy selections and placements, from which logical counts, ranks, and physical ordering can be reconstructed. Unlike the present two independent greedy stages, this directly trades replica allocation against GPU placement and can move replica budget toward experts that most reduce overloaded GPUs. This is a fundamentally stronger model when skew is concentrated and node-local expert sets contain heterogeneous loads.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Jointly minimize overload concentration caused by the interaction of replica counts and GPU placements; this can outperform greedy replication even when both use the same total number of physical experts.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This must be a true single flow construction and solve, not a sequence of threshold searches or flow-based post-processing passes. NetworkX is Python-heavy, so only use it for bounded layer/node sizes; retain the existing tensor greedy algorithm above a conservative graph-size threshold to protect runtime scoring. Costs must be nonnegative integers for robust `min_cost_flow`, so scale floating token weights deterministically and avoid overflow. Carefully enforce prefix semantics for replicas: a model must not select a third copy of an expert while omitting its first or second copy. Validate exact output invariants: every physical position assigned, every logical expert has at least one physical copy, counts match occurrences, and ranks enumerate occurrences from zero.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use torch.topk marginal replica gains to make replication explicitly bottleneck-aware and eliminate repeated full-row max reductions
tried_paradigms.description: The present `replicate_experts` repeatedly selects the maximum current per-copy expert load, which is a good water-filling approximation and likely contributes substantially to its existing score. However, it makes replica count decisions before accounting for the fact that node group assignment can strand load, and it performs one `max(dim=-1)` reduction for every redundant slot. For each logical expert, enumerate its feasible replica-count marginal improvements, where adding copy `k+1` reduces its effective load from `w/k` to `w/(k+1)`; retain the mandatory first copy separately. Flatten all candidate marginal gains within each layer/node and select exactly the redundancy budget in one `torch.topk` call. Convert selected marginal-copy indicators into counts via scatter/add or cumulative reconstruction, then create `phy2log` and ranks deterministically from those counts before using the existing placement routine. To make this more aligned with final balancing than the current rule, score each candidate by reduction relative to a node/GPU target load estimated from total node load divided by GPU count, rather than solely by raw `w/k`; this prioritizes copies that remove overload rather than spending copies on already-safe experts. This preserves the important discrete capacity constraints and reduces Python-loop synchronization, while retaining the current hierarchy where required. It is a low-risk replacement because the existing algorithm is already effectively selecting from the same decreasing marginal sequence, but `topk` makes the global choice explicit and faster.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve replication-budget allocation and reduce algorithm execution time, particularly for many redundant experts or many layers, while keeping mandatory coverage and exact replica totals.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Selecting raw marginal reduction alone optimizes total reduction, not exact maximum load; target-aware scoring should be tested against the hidden evaluator because the wrapper provides no metric details. Do not select optional copies across node boundaries in hierarchical mode unless cross-node replication is allowed by the expected policy; use one independent selection per layer/node. Floating-point ties need deterministic tie-breaking, such as a tiny expert-index-based ordering term, to avoid unstable mappings. Ensure that selecting marginal copy `k+1` implies all earlier copies; with decreasing gains, `topk` normally has this property, but equal/zero weights require an explicit prefix-safe reconstruction. The existing CPU conversion may dominate small workloads, so avoid adding expensive tensor reshapes or candidate matrices when redundancy is tiny.
